package.title: Tempo.Blazor.Reporting
package.description: Blazor reporting components for Tempo Reporting: report viewer, parameter panel, explorer, lightweight designer, embedded sources, and remote Report Server integration.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Tempo.Blazor.Reporting
gettingStarted.overview: Tempo.Blazor.Reporting provides Blazor components and services for viewing, exploring, designing, and embedding Tempo reports. It supports embedded rendering with local report definitions and remote rendering against Tempo Report Server endpoints.

programCs.description: Register Tempo.Blazor and reporting viewer services.

cssAndJs.description: The package uses Tempo.Blazor styles and ships a reporting viewer JS bundle as a static web asset.
cssAndJs.code:
<link href="_content/Tempo.Blazor/css/tempo-blazor.bundled.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<!-- The report viewer loads _content/Tempo.Blazor.Reporting/js/reporting/tm-report-viewer.bundle.js as an ES module. -->

importsRazor.description: Add reporting namespaces for convenient component usage.

notes: EmbeddedReportSource runs the reporting engine in the current Blazor render mode.
RemoteReportSource uses HTTP endpoints compatible with the report viewer-facing remote API shape.
For full Report Server catalog, revisions, render jobs, and data source administration use ITempoReportServerClient from Tempo.Reporting.Abstractions.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor
packages.description: Comprehensive Blazor component library with 100+ components. Supports WebAssembly, Server, and InteractiveAuto render modes. Multi-targets .NET 8/9/10. Includes multilingual support (EN/CS/SK/FR), CSS variable theming, and dark mode. Optional FluentValidation integration is available through Tempo.Blazor.FluentValidation.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.Spreadsheet
packages.description: Excel-like spreadsheet components for Tempo.Blazor, including canvas rendering, formula editing, workbook import/export, and spreadsheet interop assets.

packages.description: Notion-style editor components for Tempo.Blazor, including pages, blocks, databases, collaboration UI, comments, media, and Tempo embed blocks.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.All
packages.description: Compatibility package for Tempo.Blazor that references the core package and split feature packages for applications that want the full component suite.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions
packages.description: Interfaces and models for Tempo.Blazor component library. Zero UI dependencies – safe to reference from API/service projects.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.FluentValidation

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.DocumentFormats
packages.description: Optional server-side DOCX and ODT import/export support for TmDocumentEditor.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine
packages.description: Local render engine for the Tempo.Blazor email template editor: the sandboxed Scriban template engine (member policy, escaping, audit, limits), the Mjml.Net compiler, the AngleSharp HTML sanitizer, the render pipeline and the local preview renderer. Reference this package on the server (or anywhere a local render is acceptable); the editor itself (Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates) runs without it, e.g. in Blazor WebAssembly with a server-side IEmailPreviewRenderer.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Abstractions
packages.description: Logic and contracts for the Tempo.Blazor email template editor: block model, MJML generation and import, template/validation/preview contracts, variable extraction, DTOs and validators. No Blazor dependency, no Scriban/Mjml.Net/AngleSharp dependency (the local engine ships separately as Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates.Engine) – safe to reference from API/service projects and usable from Blazor WebAssembly.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.EmailTemplates
packages.description: Drag-and-drop email template editor component (TmEmailTemplateEditor) for Tempo.Blazor. Visual MJML editor with full MJML 4 parity, bidirectional MJML import/export, Scriban variable templating and live preview. Built entirely on Tempo.Blazor components.

packages.name: Tempo.Blazor.Mcp
packages.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for designing and editing Tempo.Blazor wireframes, diagrams, editor documents and reports with an LLM. Ships tools + storage abstractions only; the host application maps them onto its own MCP server.

packages.name: Tempo.Reporting.Abstractions
packages.description: Contracts, JSON definition schema, validation models, data provider interfaces, and server DTOs for Tempo Reporting. No Blazor or ASP.NET dependency.

packages.name: Tempo.Reporting.Engine
packages.description: Tempo Reporting processing engine with expression evaluation, parameter resolution, layout, snapshots, PDF/PNG rendering, and CSV/XLSX export primitives.

examples.title: Handling drill-through navigation
examples.code:
<TmReportViewer Source="@_source" TenantId="acme" UserId="@UserName" CultureName="en-US"
                OnDrillThrough="HandleDrillThrough" />

@code {
    private void HandleDrillThrough(ReportDrillThroughResolution resolution)
    {
        if (!resolution.HasTarget)
        {
            return;
        }

        // resolution.TargetReportPath / TargetReportId plus resolution.Parameters
        // carry the mapped values; the host decides how to navigate.
        Navigation.NavigateTo(ReportDeepLink.Build(resolution)!);
    }
}
